unresolved_gaps: L1: LongHorizon-Harness auditor-removal ablation never run; auditor verdict accuracy never reported (StateAct measured ~90% false-pass for the same design on the same benchmark).
L1: OSWorld comparison is not tool-matched; baseline is official GUI-only while the experimental arm uses a hybrid GUI+CLI pool.
L1: ProgressiveDisclosure has no token-matched raw arm; RecursiveAgentHarness has no ablation and no compute measurement.

L2: No single study varies verifier independence dosage (same-context / fresh-context same-backbone / cross-family / deterministic) at fixed task and fixed budget; the four dosage points sit in four different papers on four different benchmarks.
L2: Compute-matched control (spend the verification budget but discard the verdict) exists in only one work (GRASP).
L2: Stratifying gains by baseline trajectory quality is done only by TeamBench, and its strata use the same observation as the difference (uncorrected regression to the mean).
L3: No mechanism exists to detect contract misinterpretation, where independent audit hardens a confidently verified wrong answer.
L3: The negative effect of verification on already-succeeding trajectories is observed by three independent papers but its mechanism (destructive edits vs budget crowd-out) is untested.
L3: Grader validity is unresolved in TeamBench (Fleiss kappa 0.74 with the deterministic verdict shown, 0.07 hidden).

notes: Coverage is arXiv-dominant; every 'not found' statement in the report is scoped as 'within the current search range'.
GRASP carries significant weight in the evidence matrix but has no Evidence Ledger or verification_status; flagged legacy-unverified, source check recommended.
HarnessEvolution has at least four internal numeric contradictions and no public replication package; efficiency correlation usable, single-version figures are not.
The binomial-noise estimate on HarnessEvolution's 50-task per-release resolve rate is this report's calculation, not the paper's, and is labeled as such in the text.
